topics.label: Introduction to complement and its importance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing complement and explaining why it is important to study.

topics.label: Complement’s overall role in immune defence and clearance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic gives a high-level account of what complement does in immune defence and in clearing material from the body.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature and its exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions for complement components and the exceptions that make them confusing.

topics.label: C3 activation, surface attachment, and inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how C3 is activated and how its products attach to surfaces and contribute to inflammation.

topics.label: Complement recognition pathways and the activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the three recognition pathways converge on C3 activation and how local complement activity reaches the threshold for further responses.

topics.label: Complement’s downstream effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how activated complement produces downstream effects on phagocytes, immune-cell recruitment, and target membranes.

topics.label: Complement regulation and protection of host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins limit complement activity on the body’s own cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic relates deficiencies in complement components and regulators to their distinct clinical consequences.

topics.label: Complement evasion by Staphylococcus aureus and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic centers on how S. aureus evades complement, including how protein A’s antibody binding also enables clinical and laboratory uses.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the complement lecture and points to the next lecture on adaptive immunity.
